channel.name: [Concluded] GA - Repeal "Ship Recycling and Breaking Protocols"

messages.content:
Author: Solringen (Haymarket)
Co-author: Imperial Pittsburgh

Forum thread: https://forum.nationstates.net/viewtopic.php?f=9&t=568311
Proposal link: https://www.nationstates.net/page=UN_view_proposal/id=solringen_1752699015

Target resolution: https://www.nationstates.net/page=WA_past_resolution/id=627/council=1
Target forum thread: https://forum.nationstates.net/viewtopic.php?t=523295

Replacement: lol what year do you think this is

Cast your vote by reacting to this message. You can also discuss below. Information here may be used to construct an IFV.

:tep_for:  = FOR / AYE
:tep_against:  = AGAINST / NAY
:tep_abstain:  = TEP ABSTAINS
:tep_present:  = NO OPINION / PRESENT
Target is classic Simone hyperspecificity
In other words, I don't really care whether this gets repealed or not lol
I'm only opposed to the repeal because it argues that wood doesn't need to be recycled, which is a stupid argument. It's like saying that paper doesn't need to be recycled.
Writing guy coulda thought to take 2 seconds to search and realize paper is able to be recycled
We don’t account for ships made of paper in the repeal, so it’s recyclability is irrelevant

What we meant by that, is that from a standpoint of ecological health, wooden ships can be safely sunk and cause minimal adverse effects to the environment around them, which is not the case for all shipbuilding materials

I don't think that is necessarily the case? Wooden ships can last for a very long time, and while I'm uncertain as to the impact they have on aquatic environments (I'm not a marine biologist), I can say for certain that sinking wooden ships instead of recycling the materials is certainly not the most ecologically sound practice.
In many cases they’re beneficial to underwater environments, and can be used to form artificial reefs
So can metal ships, no?
On top of that if used responsibly, wood is a renewable resource
As long as it’s not made of harmful material and it can last
So then why point to wood specifically as a material that doesn't need to be recycled if metal ships can also be used as artificial reefs?
It was an example
It was also highlighting that the target requires intricate plans for recycling ships like they’re made of solid asbestos
When wood simply does not require that level of care
I'm gonna go with both wood and metal need to be recycled, honestly.
Wood is a renewable resource
Also I think that this isn't really all that accurate. Wood still requires matter, the matter has to come from somewhere. It's no more renewable than metal.
That’s outrageous
You can plant more trees
We can make wood basically as long as we have the sun
Wood contains carbon
Where do they get the carbon from?
Have you ever heard of the carbon cycle
Notice how fossil fuels are in this. Do you think those are a renewable resource too?
They aren’t, but notice how they aren’t in the loop
Trees have been growing for roughly 450 million years and they haven’t run out of carbon yet
They are? When fossil fuels are burned in auto and factory emissions, it adds carbon dioxide to the atmosphere, which is removed by trees and other organisms.
And they are generated by decaying organic matter.
They are part of the carbon cycle.
Fossil fuels are non-renewable because they take millions of years to form, and the conditions that allowed them to form en mass don’t exist anymkore
Aka there’s no producer for them
Now point to me where on this that carbon leaves the system

It doesn't. It never leaves the system for fossil fuels *or* trees, and there's no reasonable difference between trees and fossil fuels. 

If we switched entirely over to wood burning stoves and burning wood to power factories (which would be ridiculously inefficient, mind you) what do you think would happen? We solved climate change?
Ok so we’ve established that carbon is renewable correct?
No.
Point to me where carbon leaves the system then
Or where the cycle stops
Hint: it doesn’t, trees won’t run out of carbon
We can keep growing them
Therefore wood is renewable
Okay so where does literally any type matter (except I guess radioactive materials which decay) we use leave the Earth's system?
Obviously there’s a limit to our production of it, but it is a renewable resource
So your point is, that because it’s technically possible across millions or billions of years for the carbon cycle to eventually run dry, wood is non-renewable
This entire argument could’ve been avoided by googling “is wood renewable”
It's not going to take millions of years for deforestation to occur.
It's already occurring.
When you don’t practice sustainable logging, you can and many places do
But wood is just as non-renewable as iron right
Do you understand the relationship between demand for logging and how much wood gets recycled?
If you stop recycling wood, you're gonna need to cut down more trees.
I don’t think you understand, we have to, or at least should recycle stuff like iron or aluminum and stuff cause that’s all we have, once we run out we have to go to space to get more
That is not a problem with wood
Because it literally grows on trees

The Earth has a more or less fixed amount of iron, aluminium, and titanium in much the same way it has a more or less fixed amount of carbon. 

Unless you think we can make carbon fiber boats indefinitely
Any wood that is not recycled ends up back in the carbon cycle
Eventually.
So does fossil fuel.
The problem is how fast?
As eventually as anything else does
So everything is renewable?
Plants are
What do you think happens to an iron boat that isn't recycled? It gets sucked into a black hole?
It doesn’t magically form into a new vein of iron to mine
Technically that's not necessarily true?
This is such a huge stretch, though I appreciate your dedication

The iron will eventually rust. The sediment may settle on the sea floor. The tectonic plate subduction may carry it into the mantle, and volcanic flows can form iron veins. 

This is obviously an incredibly slow and not guaranteed process.
It would be much faster to just recycle the iron.
Likewise, we could plant new trees and wait 20 years for them to grow or we could just recycle the wood ships we built.

Also, there is a wood shipwreck off Burgas, Bulgaria dating back to [400 BC](https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-45951132) , so if you want to count waiting 2400 years for a ship's wood to reenter the carbon cycle as renewable, be my guest.

embeds.title: Shipwreck found in Black Sea is 'world's oldest intact'
embeds.description: A Greek merchant ship dating back more than 2,400 years is found almost perfectly preserved.

messages.content: A wonderful lack of understanding
The amount of carbon contained in that ship is basically a rounding error
Also
It’s a god damn planet wide cycle
If it was stopped by a small amount of wood being preserved for a few thousand years it would’ve died eons ago
Goodness Gracious Me, how did this turn into a whole DEBATE?
Because wood is a non renewable resource apparently
Healthy debate about a resolution
Sure, but the same goes for the amount of iron on a steel vessel. Earth is like, 5% iron or something. That's a huge amount.
Either way this is huge distraction from the real issue
Not recycling an easily recyclable material like wood is wasteful.
Regardless, this seems like a non-issue in the scope of the repeal

If one of the repeal's main arguments is that some ships are built out of materials that don't need to be recycled, but the only example given is of a material that should be recycled, that seems like a big enough issue to me.
“We, erm, we will be voting no.”
